title: App Connector health, status values and telemetry

checks.do: Whether Connection Health, the Status log SessionStatus and the control session agree, using the Status log rather than M-Tunnel counts to judge whether the connector is connected.
Whether AliveTargetCount trails TargetCount for the connector in question.

connection-health-column.statement: The App Connectors page shows each connector's Connection Health as Connected or Disconnected, separately from its Status (enabled or disabled).

quotes: Connection Health: The health of the App Connector connection (Connected or Disconnected).
Status: Indicates whether the App Connector is enabled or disabled.

disconnected-year-alert.statement: If any connectors have been disconnected for a year or more, an alert on Admin Console login links to a page filtered to them for review or deletion.

quotes: If any App Connectors have been disconnected for one year or more, an alert appears when you log in to the Zscaler Admin Console.
Click the number of disconnected App Connectors in the alert to open this page, which is filtered by the disconnected App Connectors so you can review or delete them.

status-log-control-session.statement: The App Connector Status log's SessionType is ZPN_ASSISTANT_BROKER_CONTROL, the session from the connector to the closest Public Service Edge, and SessionStatus is one of ZPN_STATUS_AUTHENTICATED, ZPN_STATUS_AUTH_FAILED or ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED.

quotes: The expected value for this field is ZPN_ASSISTANT_BROKER_CONTROL, which denotes the session from the App Connector towards the closest Public Service Edge for Private Access.
ZPN_STATUS_AUTHENTICATED: App Connector successfully authenticated in Private Access
ZPN_STATUS_AUTH_FAILED: App Connector failed to authenticate in Private Access
ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED: App Connector disconnected from a Service Edge for Private Access
The status of the session. The expected values for this field are:
ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED: App Connector disconnected from a Service Edge for Private Access |

metrics-target-counts.statement: The App Connector Metrics log reports TargetCount, the targets configured for access via the connector, and AliveTargetCount, the targets alive for access via it.

quotes: TargetCount | The number of targets configured for access via this App Connector
AliveTargetCount | The number of targets alive for access via this App Connector

alive-below-target.statement: AliveTargetCount below TargetCount means some configured targets are not alive for access via that connector at that time.
alive-below-target.conditions: Reads the two definitions together; the help does not interpret the difference.

metrics-mtunnel-counts.statement: The metrics log counts active and disconnected Microtunnel (M-Tunnel) connections separately to Public and Private Service Edges (ActiveConnectionsToPublicSE, DisconnectedConnectionsToPublicSE, ActiveConnectionsToPrivateSE, DisconnectedConnectionsToPrivateSE).

quotes: ActiveConnectionsToPublicSE | The number of active Microtunnel (M-Tunnel) connections to the Public Service Edge for Private Access
DisconnectedConnectionsToPublicSE | The number of disconnected Microtunnel (M-Tunnel) connections to the Public Service Edge
ActiveConnectionsToPrivateSE | The number of active Microtunnel (M-Tunnel) connections to the Private Service Edge for Private Access
DisconnectedConnectionsToPrivateSE | The number of disconnected Microtunnel (M-Tunnel) connections to the Private Service Edge

health-reporting-values.statement: An application segment's health_reporting accepts NONE, ON_ACCESS or CONTINUOUS.

quotes: Whether health reporting for the app is Continuous or On Access. Supported values: NONE, ON_ACCESS, CONTINUOUS.

control-channel-field.statement: Both SDKs expose the connector's control-connection state as controlChannelStatus (Python control_channel_status, Go ControlChannelStatus).

quotes: self.control_channel_status = config["controlChannelStatus"] if "controlChannelStatus" in config else None
ControlChannelStatus string `json:"controlChannelStatus,omitempty"`

no-runtime-status-field.statement: Neither SDK nor the Terraform provider defines a field named runtime_status or runtimeStatus for connectors; that name and the ZPN_STATUS_* table used with it appear in the MCP server's skill and command markdown.
no-runtime-status-field.conditions: Rests on a case-insensitive search of vendor/zscaler-sdk-python, vendor/zscaler-sdk-go and vendor/terraform-provider-zpa for runtime_status and runtimeStatus that found no match.

mcp-status-table.statement: The MCP troubleshooting skill's connector status table gives ZPN_STATUS_AUTHENTICATED as healthy, ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED as lost connection, ZPN_STATUS_NOT_ENROLLED as never enrolled or enrollment failed, and ZPN_STATUS_PENDING as enrollment in progress; the command document lists only the first three.

quotes: | `ZPN_STATUS_AUTHENTICATED` | Healthy, control connection established |
| `ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED` | Lost connection to ZPA cloud |
| `ZPN_STATUS_NOT_ENROLLED` | Never enrolled or enrollment failed |
| `ZPN_STATUS_PENDING` | Enrollment in progress |
`ZPN_STATUS_NOT_ENROLLED` = enrollment failed
Check `runtime_status`: - `ZPN_STATUS_AUTHENTICATED` = healthy - `ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED` = lost connection - `ZPN_STATUS_NOT_ENROLLED` = enrollment failed Also check `current_version`

lss-status-set-differs.statement: The LSS SessionStatus list includes ZPN_STATUS_AUTH_FAILED, which is not in the MCP connector status table, so the two lists are not identical (they share AUTHENTICATED and DISCONNECTED).
lss-status-set-differs.conditions: Compares the two code lists; no source states how the MCP field maps to LSS. Statement changed from 'different families of codes' because the lists overlap.

lss-codes-fetched.statement: The Python SDK retrieves LSS session status codes from the API, filtered by log type, rather than defining them as constants, so the full set cannot be listed from SDK source.

quotes: Returns a list of LSS Session Status Codes filtered by log type.

control-channel-status-values.statement: The OpenAPI connector GET response marks controlChannelStatus read-only and enumerates UNKNOWN, ZPN_STATUS_AUTHENTICATED and ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED.

expect.description: Read only. Ignored in PUT/POST calls. Expected values: UNKNOWN/ZPN_STATUS_AUTHENTICATED(1)/ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED

control-channel-status-values.conditions: Added from the verifier's finding: the enum had been dropped as generated, but the generated surface holds no enums.

upgrade-status-values.statement: The OpenAPI connector GET response enumerates upgradeStatus as COMPLETE, IN_PROGRESS, FAILED, UNKNOWN, RESTARTING, PARTIAL_FAILURE and REMOVAL_IN_PROGRESS, and each zpnSubModuleUpgradeList entry's role as ASSISTANT, PRIVATE_BROKER, MMDB_GEOIP, MMDB_ISP, GUACD and SITE_CONTROLLER.
upgrade-status-values.conditions: Added from the verifier's finding: the enums had been dropped as generated, but the generated surface holds no enums.

connector-object-fields.statement: The Python connector model carries current and expected version, last upgrade time, last broker connect and disconnect times with durations, platform and Sarge upgrade fields, all read from the response.

quotes: self.current_version = config["currentVersion"] if "currentVersion" in config else None
self.expected_version = config["expectedVersion"] if "expectedVersion" in config else None
self.last_upgrade_time = config["lastUpgradeTime"] if "lastUpgradeTime" in config else None
self.last_broker_connect_time = config["lastBrokerConnectTime"] if "lastBrokerConnectTime" in config else None
self.sarge_upgrade_status = config["sargeUpgradeStatus"] if "sargeUpgradeStatus" in config else None
self.last_broker_connect_time_duration = ( config["lastBrokerConnectTimeDuration"] if "lastBrokerConnectTimeDuration" in config else None )
self.last_broker_disconnect_time = ( config["lastBrokerDisconnectTime"] if "lastBrokerDisconnectTime" in config else None )
self.last_broker_disconnect_time_duration = ( config["lastBrokerDisconnectTimeDuration"] if "lastBrokerDisconnectTimeDuration" in config else None )
self.platform = config["platform"] if "platform" in config else None

cert-expiry-in-status-output.statement: A running connector periodically writes a status line to the local logs that includes how long its certificate has left.

quotes: Certificate will expire in 370 days, 21 hours, 39 minutes

pause-reasons.statement: A connector can be paused for certificate expiry, software upgrade, session process restart or session system restart; it logs 'entering PAUSE mode because of' with the reason, and a paused connector can reject remote session commands.

quotes: PAUSE_REASON_CERT_EXPIRY: Certificate expiry
PAUSE_REASON_UPGRADE: Software upgrade
sudo journalctl | grep "entering PAUSE mode because of"
entity is currently in paused mode, not taking any probe commands
PAUSE_REASON_ADMIN_PROBE_PROCESS_RESTART: Session process restart
PAUSE_REASON_ADMIN_PROBE_SYSTEM_RESTART: Session system restart

pause-reasons.conditions: Statement changed from 'rejects' to 'can reject', matching the help's 'might reject additional session commands'.

logged-but-disconnected.statement: A connector that logged a successful connection but shows as disconnected in the Admin Console most likely is not getting CPU cycles or its VM is frozen; stopping and restarting the VM is the suggested remedy.

quotes: there is most likely an issue with the connector process not getting CPU cycles on the virtual machine (VM) or the VM is frozen.
To resolve this issue, try stopping the VM and restarting it again.
If an App Connector successfully logged a connection but the App Connector shows as disconnected in the Zscaler Admin Console

cloud-connectivity-checks.statement: For a connector that cannot reach the cloud, the help checks that the firewall allows the published Private Access address ranges, that co2br.prod.zpath.net resolves to two addresses, and that an openssl TLS connection to a Public Service Edge returns a certificate subject.

quotes: Successful connectivity results in two IP addresses.
A successful TLS connection results in a certificate subject string returned from the Public Service Edge.
Make sure all the IP address ranges allowed by the firewall match those in the Private Access firewall policies
Test connectivity to the upstream Public Service Edge for Private Access by querying the DNS address co2br.prod.zpath.net
Test if the App Connector can make a TLS connection to a Public Service Edge using the openssl command.
Make sure all the IP address ranges allowed by the firewall match those in the Private Access firewall policies: config.zscaler.com/private.zscaler.com/zpa

lss-retransmit-limits.statement: After a connection loss between Private Access and the App Connectors, LSS does not send the log data generated during the loss and can retransmit only the last 15 minutes after restoration, with delivery not guaranteed; during a loss between the App Connector and the SIEM, LSS sends nothing for that period except audit logs.

quotes: The LSS does not transmit any log data generated during a connection loss between Private Access and the App Connectors. After the connection is restored, it can retransmit the last 15 minutes of the log data. However, the delivery of that log data is not guaranteed.
With the exception of audit log data, the LSS does not transmit any log data generated during a connection loss between the App Connector and the SIEM.

status-pending-unverified.title: ZPN_STATUS_PENDING as a real status
status-pending-unverified.detail: Tracked as legacy ledger item zpa-20. The value appears only in one table of the MCP skill; it is absent from the command document, from SDK source, and from the status-log-field articles. The contract's connector response enumerates controlChannelStatus as UNKNOWN, ZPN_STATUS_AUTHENTICATED and ZPN_STATUS_DISCONNECTED (control-channel-status-values), with no PENDING value; whether a pending state appears in another field is not shown.

not-enrolled-vs-pending.title: What distinguishes NOT_ENROLLED from PENDING
not-enrolled-vs-pending.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "No source defines what controlChannelStatus/runtime_status value distinguishes these states at the API level; the meanings are prose in SKILL.md tables only, not from a server enum." The full set cannot be listed from SDK source because the codes are fetched at runtime (lss-codes-fetched). The contract's connector response enum for controlChannelStatus (control-channel-status-values) has neither a NOT_ENROLLED nor a PENDING value, so neither state is a controlChannelStatus value in the contract.

health-reporting-cadence.title: How often health_reporting probes run
health-reporting-cadence.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The probe cadence depends on the segment's health_reporting: NONE = probe only at access time; ON_ACCESS = probe at access, cache result; CONTINUOUS = probe on a regular cadence regardless of access." The help defines the three values as reporting continuously (Continuous), while a user is accessing it (On Access) or not at all (None) (see zpa.app-segments.settings:health-reporting-default), so the legacy 'NONE = probe only at access time' is contradicted: None is not at all. How often probing runs under Continuous or On Access is still unstated.

cert-or-firewall-disconnect.title: Disconnected connector with a running VM
cert-or-firewall-disconnect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Connector says DISCONNECTED even though the VM is running - certificate expired (if connector has been running >cert validity), or outbound firewall blocking cloud reach." The help supports paused-for-certificate-expiry (pause-reasons) and the connectivity checks (cloud-connectivity-checks) but never ties a Disconnected status to an expired certificate or gives the validity period.
